title: Plant transport: xylem and transpiration; Limiting factors and rate of photosynthesis; Human gas exchange and ventilation
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for CCEA A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: EX02a#t4 term and clue written for the game; EX02a#t2 term and clue written for the game; PS04#t1 term and clue written for the game; EX02a#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: EX02a#N.6, EX10b#N.10a, PS04#N.3, EX02a#N.11, PS04#N.8.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Internal intercostal muscles
items.clue: Contract only in forced breathing out, pulling the ribs down and in

items.label: Surfactant
items.clue: Substance in the moist lining of the air sacs that stops them collapsing

items.label: Limiting factor
items.clue: The variable in shortest supply, which alone sets the rate of photosynthesis.

items.label: Diaphragm
items.clue: Muscle below the lungs that contracts, flattens and moves down when breathing in

questions.stem: Mammalian lungs contain a branched network of bronchioles ending in millions of alveoli. How does this branching contribute to gas exchange?

options.text: It multiplies the area of airway wall across which gases are exchanged into the blood as air travels inward.
It packs a very large alveolar surface, each part close to a capillary bed, into the volume of the thorax.
It lets the lungs grow larger, and a larger organ must have a bigger surface for gas exchange.
It houses the muscle that contracts to pump air in and out of the alveoli found at the end of every branch.

questions.stem: A grower's greenhouse plants wilt on hot afternoons. The grower wants to slow their transpiration. Which change would do this?

options.text: Switch on fans to blow air over the leaves, because cooler leaves lose less water.
Water the soil more, so that the plants no longer need to transpire as much.
Dry the greenhouse air, because humid air keeps the leaves wet and speeds water loss.
Mist the air to raise the humidity, so the water-vapour gradient is smaller.

questions.explanation: Less difference between the air spaces and the air means slower diffusion of water vapour out of the stomata.

questions.stem: Pondweed submerged in water at 25 °C with the carbon dioxide concentration of ordinary air was exposed to increasing light intensity. The rate of photosynthesis rose at first and then levelled off, staying constant however much the light intensity was increased. Which change is most likely to raise the rate at this plateau?

options.text: Moving the lamp even closer, so that the light intensity becomes higher still.
Adding sodium hydrogencarbonate to the water to raise the carbon dioxide concentration.
Nothing, because the plateau is the maximum rate of which the plant is capable.
Adding more water to the beaker, since water is a reactant in photosynthesis.

questions.stem: Which sequence of events draws air into the lungs during inspiration?

options.text: Air entering the lungs inflates them, and the inflating lungs push the ribs outward and the diaphragm downward.
The muscular walls of the lungs contract, widening the alveoli and sucking air in through the trachea.
The diaphragm and external intercostals contract, thorax volume rises and lung pressure falls.
The diaphragm relaxes and rises into a dome, and the ribs move up so that air is drawn in to fill the space.

questions.explanation: Larger thorax volume, pressure in the lungs below atmospheric, and air flows in down the pressure gradient.

questions.stem: A student places a lamp at different distances from a beaker of pondweed in sodium hydrogencarbonate solution kept at 25 °C, and counts the bubbles of gas released per minute at each distance. Which correctly identifies the variables?

options.text: Independent: lamp distance; dependent: bubbles per minute
Independent: bubbles per minute; dependent: distance of lamp
Controlled variable: lamp distance; dependent: bubbles per minute
Independent: temperature of 25 °C; dependent: bubbles per minute

questions.explanation: Lamp distance is deliberately changed (it sets light intensity): independent. Bubble count is measured: dependent. Temperature and hydrogencarbonate concentration are controlled.
